evals.prompt: Store the Cloudinary secure_url from the upload response on the post record, and build thumbnails as https://res.cloudinary.com/demo/image/upload/c_fill,w_400,f_auto,q_auto/v1712/blog-covers/post-42.jpg.
evals.expected_output: Should store the public id and its version, never a URL, and build every URL in one server-side helper when the record is read. `f_auto` and `q_auto` each go in their own final component — `c_fill,g_auto,w_400/f_auto/q_auto` — never merged into the resize step. A fixed-shape slot uses `c_fill,g_auto` so the crop follows the subject.
expectations: Stores the public id and version, not the URL
Puts f_auto and q_auto in their own components at the end
Uses g_auto for the fixed-shape crop

evals.prompt: Add a /api/cloudinary/sign route that takes the params from the request body and returns cloudinary.utils.api_sign_request(body, secret), so the browser can upload directly.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse signing whatever the request sends. The route sits behind the session guard and a rate limit, and signs only server-chosen parameters — public id, asset_folder, timestamp, allowed formats and size (or a signed preset), so it can't take an SVG. The server verifies the upload response's signature before recording the public id and version. The secret stays server-only.
expectations: Requires a session guard and a rate limit
Signs only server-chosen parameters, including allowed formats

evals.prompt: We need to tweak the card thumbnail crop. I'll edit the t_card_v1 named transformation in the console and add f_auto inside it.
evals.expected_output: Should ship the change as `t_card_v2`, created by an idempotent script, because the CDN keeps renders made with the old definition; remove `t_card_v1` once nothing uses it. `f_auto` inside a named transformation is ignored — it follows the name: `t_card_v2/f_auto/q_auto`.
expectations: Creates a new versioned name instead of editing
Uses a script, not the console
Says f_auto inside a named transformation is ignored

evals.prompt: Set up next/image for our Cloudinary blog. Put a loader in images.loaderFile so every image goes through Cloudinary automatically.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse `images.loaderFile`, which rewrites every image on the site. The components that show Cloudinary images pass a per-image `loader` that only adds the width to the URL the server built, and `images.deviceSizes` is set to the width ladder (e.g. 480, 768, 1024, 1280, 1600) so the widths and their billed derivatives stay bounded.
expectations: Sets deviceSizes to the width ladder
Links bounded widths to transformation cost
